title: Refund policy
text: Customers can request a refund within 30 days of purchase. Refunds are returned to the original payment method. Card refunds usually appear within 5 to 10 business days, depending on the issuing bank. Purchases older than 30 days are not eligible for a refund, but they may qualify for store credit.

title: Chargebacks and disputes
text: A chargeback happens when a cardholder disputes a payment with their bank. Merchants have 7 days to submit evidence after a chargeback notice. Accepted evidence includes delivery confirmation, signed receipts and customer correspondence. A chargeback fee of 15 USD is charged for every dispute, whether or not the merchant wins.

title: Merchant payouts
text: Payouts are sent to the merchant's verified bank account every business day. New merchants have a 7 day rolling reserve during their first 90 days. Payouts are paused if the bank account fails verification or if the account is under compliance review.

title: Identity verification (KYC)
text: Every merchant must complete identity verification before receiving payouts. Individuals provide a government-issued photo ID and proof of address issued within the last 3 months. Businesses also provide registration documents and the details of every beneficial owner holding 25 percent or more.

title: Processing fees
text: Domestic card payments cost 2.9 percent plus 0.30 USD per successful transaction. International cards add 1.5 percent. Currency conversion adds 1 percent. There are no monthly fees and no setup fees.

title: Account security
text: Two-factor authentication is required for every dashboard user with payout permissions. API keys can be restricted by IP address and should be rotated at least every 90 days. Secret keys must never be embedded in mobile apps or browser code.

title: Data retention
text: Transaction records are retained for 7 years to meet financial record-keeping obligations. Full card numbers are never stored; only the last four digits and a token are kept. Customers can request deletion of personal data that is not subject to a legal retention requirement.

title: Idempotent requests
text: Payment requests accept an Idempotency-Key header. Retrying a request with the same key returns the original result instead of creating a second charge. Keys expire after 24 hours. Reusing a key with a different request body returns an error.

title: Webhooks
text: Webhook events are signed with a shared secret so the receiver can verify they are genuine. Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to 3 days. Receivers should process events idempotently because the same event can be delivered more than once.

title: Rate limits
text: The API allows 100 read requests and 50 write requests per second per account. Requests over the limit receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Clients should back off and retry rather than fail immediately.
